title: Cabinet Refinishing in Chiefland, FL | Kitchen Update
description: Cabinet refinishing in Chiefland, FL that holds up to humid kitchens: degreased, scuff-sanded, primed, and sprayed with waterborne urethane enamel.
heroIntro: A refinished kitchen that will not start peeling the first humid summer. We focus on the adhesion steps that DIY cabinet paint jobs usually skip.

questions: Why is the paint peeling off my kitchen cabinets?
Should I refinish or replace my cabinets?
What finish holds up best on cabinets?

sections.h2: Why cabinet paint fails in damp kitchens
body: Peeling cabinet paint almost always comes back to adhesion. Grease from cooking, moisture around the sink, and a smooth factory finish that was never sanded all keep paint from gripping. In a humid town like Chiefland, steam from cooking and dishwashers adds to it. Cabinet refinishing in Chiefland, FL is about fixing that bond before any color goes on.
Living with flaking doors right now? We put together some stopgap repairs for peeling cabinet paint to tide your Chiefland kitchen over until the real refinish.

sections.h2: The adhesion steps we never skip
bullets: Take off every door, drawer face, hinge, and pull, tagging each one to its opening
Degrease every surface, including the inside edges near handles
Rough up the old glossy finish with sandpaper to give the primer tooth
Repair dents, chips, and loose joints
Finish with a pair of sprayed waterborne urethane enamel coats

body: Waterborne urethane enamel dries to a hard, cleanable surface that resists the knocks and spills of a working kitchen. It also levels out smoothly when sprayed, so you get a factory-like look instead of brush marks. We trust it on entry doors and stair railings for the same reason: hands and bumps do not wear it down quickly. A low-VOC version can be specified as well.

Sandpaper does not touch a single box until the counters, backsplash, appliances, and floor are wrapped and the kitchen is closed off with plastic from the rest of your home. The cabinet boxes themselves stay mounted and are coated right where they are installed. Your quote lays out the days for each phase, and a labelled jar of the cabinet color stays behind for any future nick. On the final walk, you point out anything that bothers you, and it gets corrected before we call the kitchen finished.

Sturdy boxes in a floor plan you like are a strong case for refinishing. Swollen particleboard under the sink, shelves that sag, or a layout you have never liked point toward replacement instead. Our crew lead will give you a straight answer about where your Chiefland kitchen falls, and our post on whether to refinish or replace kitchen cabinets walks through the trade-offs.

Want to keep the current shade or copy one from elsewhere in the house? A swatch, one of the doors, or a half-used can is enough for us to match, and you judge the result on a big drawdown held up in your own kitchen light. More on the service lives on our cabinet painting and refinishing page, and the Chiefland painters page lists everything else we do in town.

faqs.q: Will refinished cabinets peel in a humid Chiefland kitchen?
faqs.a: Not if the grease is stripped, the old finish is scuffed, and a bonding primer is down before the urethane enamel. Skipping those steps is what usually causes peeling.

faqs.q: Can you refinish bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Add the bathroom vanity, a laundry cabinet, or built-in shelving to the kitchen quote and we will coat them in the matching enamel.

faqs.q: Can you match a color from one of my existing cabinet doors?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand one door to the crew lead and we will mix to it; you see the match on a full-size sample board before any spraying.

faqs.q: Are low-odor products available for cabinet work?
faqs.a: Yes. We can use low-VOC primer and enamel, a real comfort when your family is eating and sleeping a room away from the work.
